token.d: The basic unit the model reads and writes: a piece of text (word, subword, byte) or a special marker, identified by an integer (the id). Context, KV cache and speed are all measured in tokens.

tokenizador.d: The program that converts text into token ids and back. In the three recipe models it is a byte-level BPE described in tokenizer.json (vocabulary, merge rules, pre-tokenization and added tokens).

vocabulario.d: The set of all tokens the model knows; its size \(V\) (vocab_size) is the number of rows of the embedding and of the lm_head. GLM 154,880, Qwen 248,320, DeepSeek 129,280 (padding included).

utf-8.d: An encoding of text as bytes: ASCII uses 1 byte per character, accented letters 2 ("ç" = C3 A7), ideograms 3, emojis 4. Byte-level tokenizers start from these 256 values, so no text is left without a representation.

fertilidade.d: The ratio between the number of tokens and the number of words in a text. It depends on the language and the domain; the DeepSeek recipe measured 1.564 tok/word on an English text (340,787 words → 533,110 tokens).

bpe.d: A tokenization method that starts from the base alphabet (256 bytes, in byte-level BPE) and repeatedly merges the most frequent neighboring pair in the corpus, creating a new token with each merge. To encode, it applies the merges in the order they were learned; that is why low ids tend to be frequent tokens.

fusao-bpe.d: A rule “a + b → ab” learned while training the tokenizer. The merge list is ordered: when encoding, the oldest available merge is applied first. GLM's tokenizer.json carries 321,649 rules.

pre-tokenizacao.d: Cutting the text into pieces with a regular expression before BPE (words with their leading space, numbers, punctuation). Merges never cross these cuts. In the GPT-4 style, used by GLM, digits are grouped up to 3 at a time.

lei-de-zipf.d: In natural language, an item's frequency falls roughly with the inverse of its rank, \( f(r) \propto r^{-s} \) with \( s \approx 1 \): a few tokens (or N-grams) are very frequent and most are rare. It justifies reduced draft vocabularies and explains why rare tokens get little training.

token-adicionado.d: An entry in the added_tokens list of tokenizer.json: a string the tokenizer recognizes whole, before BPE, and maps to a fixed id. Only the ones with special: true vanish on detokenization; the others, like <think> in GLM (154841), show up in the text and depend on the reasoning parser.

token-especial.d: An added token (recognized whole, before BPE, with a fixed id) that carries the special: true flag in tokenizer.json. The flag decides the way back: with skip_special_tokens, it vanishes from the returned text. E.g., GLM's <|user|>, Qwen's <|image_pad|>. It marks boundaries, roles, media and draft positions.

token-bos.d: The marker for the start of a sequence. DeepSeek-V4: <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜> = id 0. In Qwen3.8 the config declares BOS = EOS = 248044 (<|endoftext|>). GLM opens the prompt with [gMASK]<sop>.

token-eos.d: The token that ends generation (finish_reason: stop). It can be a list: GLM [154820, 154827, 154829] (<|endoftext|>, <|user|>, <|observation|>), Qwen [248046, 248044], DeepSeek 1 (<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>).

padding-de-vocabulario.d: Extra rows, which no text produces, that round \(V\) up to a convenient multiple: \( V' = \lceil V/L \rceil L \), with \(L = 64\) in vLLM and \( L = \text{lcm}(64, \text{TP}) = 192 \) in the TP=3 patches (GLM 154,880 → 154,944; DeepSeek 129,280 → 129,408).

glitch-token.d: A token that is in the vocabulary but rare or absent in the model's training data. Its embedding row stays near its initialization (only tokens that are seen receive gradient at the input), and feeding it to the model can cause bizarre behavior.

chat-template.d: The function that turns the list of messages (roles, tools, media) into the text with special tokens that the model saw in training, ending with the generation prompt. It is usually Jinja in the checkpoint; DeepSeek-V4 uses a Python encoder (encoding_dsv4.py).

jinja.d: A Python templating language used in Hugging Face chat templates. The GLM recipe's template uses the loopcontrols extension ({% break %}), and the launcher parses it with Jinja2 (a syntax check, with no rendering) before the restart.

generation-prompt.d: The header the template appends at the end of the prompt (add_generation_prompt) to open the assistant's turn: <|assistant|><think> in GLM, <|im_start|>assistant in Qwen, <｜Assistant｜><think> in DeepSeek. Without it, the model generates from a state it never saw in training.

encoder-de-chat.d: A Python program in the checkpoint that plays the role of the chat template: in DeepSeek-V4, encoding/encoding_dsv4.py (encode_messages, render_message), installed by the recipe as vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4_encoding.py.

tokenizer-mode.d: The vLLM argument that picks the tokenization and chat-rendering path: auto, cohere, deepseek_v32, deepseek_v4, hf, inkling, kimi_k3, mistral, slow. The DeepSeek recipe uses deepseek_v4, which calls the checkpoint's Python encoder instead of Jinja.

endpoint-tokenize.d: A vLLM server route (at the root, not under /v1) that returns the ids and the count for a prompt or for messages rendered by the template. It does not go through the /v1 authentication.

embedding.d: The table \( E \in \mathbb{R}^{V\times d} \) that swaps each token id for the vector in its row: \( \mathbf x_t = E[i_t] \). Implemented as a lookup (gather), it reads only \(d\) numbers per token. It is the first state of the residual stream.

one-hot.d: A vector of size \(V\) with a single 1 (at the id's position) and zeros everywhere else. \( \mathbf e_i^\top E \) is row \(i\) of the embedding: the same computation as the lookup, written as a matrix product.

similaridade-cosseno.d: \( \langle \mathbf a, \mathbf b\rangle / (\lVert \mathbf a\rVert\,\lVert \mathbf b\rVert) \in [-1,1] \): the cosine of the angle between two vectors, independent of their lengths. It measures how close embeddings are; in quantization, how well the quantized tensor lines up with the original.

lm-head.d: The model's last matrix, \( W_U \in \mathbb{R}^{V\times d} \), which projects the final hidden state onto the \(V\) logits (\( \mathbf z = W_U \mathbf h \)). Every read costs \( V\cdot d\cdot 2 \) bytes in BF16: 1.27 GB (1.18 GiB) in GLM and Qwen, 1.06 GB (0.99 GiB) in DeepSeek. In none of the three models is it tied to the embedding.

embeddings-amarrados.d: Using the same matrix at the input and the output (\( W_U = E \), tie_word_embeddings: true), which saves \(V\cdot d\) parameters. The three recipe models use false: separate matrices.

modelo-bigrama.d: A model that predicts the next token from the current one alone: a \(V\times V\) transition table. A Transformer with no layers, \( \mathbf z = W_U E[x_t] \), is a bigram model of rank \(\le d\); DSpark's Markov head is a rank-256 bigram.
